paper_metadata.title: Clinical and Electroencephalographic Follow-up After a First Unprovoked Seizure

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the target population, recruitment setting, and inclusion criteria. The sample was recruited consecutively, which minimizes selection bias, and baseline characteristics are well-documented.

items.evidence_snippet: 109 children and adolescents age 1 month to 16 years who were consecutively observed 24 to 72 hours after the seizure at the Epilepsy Outpatient Service, Hospital de Clı´nicas de Porto Alegre, Brazil
items.reasoning: The authors specify the age range, clinical setting, and geographic location of the source population.

items.reasoning: Clear inclusion criteria regarding seizure type and medication status are provided.

items.reasoning: The denominator for the results remains 109, implying all patients were accounted for at the 24-month mark.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (seizure recurrence) was primarily based on family reports during scheduled visits. While standard in clinical practice, this introduces potential recall bias compared to objective monitoring.

items.evidence_snippet: investigated recurrence of seizures... based on family report
items.reasoning: Reliance on family reports for recurrence is common but less reliable than clinical observation or diary-based methods.
